info.title: MyLINK EMAIL API
info.description:
Purpose and functionality

MyLINK EMAIL API is a REST-based API that supports sending email messages to the recipients you want to reach.

Current supported functionality (high-level)

  • Send Simple Email
  • Send Email with attachments
  • Send Email with CC & BCC

Generating credentials

To generate credentials for the rest API as well as the SMTP connection, head over to MyLINK. Simply go to the Messaging APIs page in the navigation menu, select the product and generate your credentials.

Getting started

To maximise the deliverability of your emails first you need to make sure that your configuration is correctly set up. The following steps are crucial for the success of your integration:

  • Add your Domain configuration via MyLINK: doing this will give you a DKIM signature that you must add to your DNS configuration.
  • Set up your Return-path: communication back to the email server is through the return-path, make sure to add our CNAME in order for us to receive requests.
  • Set up your SPF: this will set the mail servers that are allowed to send emails on behalf of your domain.
  • Add an MX Record: Make sure an email server is used on the domain and your sender address is an existing email address to maximize deliverability. This step is not mandatory for sending but it will increase the delivery rate
All needed values for the configuration can be found on the Messaging APIs page in MyLINK. Once ready, revisit the developer portal for how to send Emails.

Limitations

  • Individual email messages sent through myLINK Email cannot exceed 15mb in size (attachments included) for API requests and 10mb for SMTP requests.
  • Multiple email messages can be sent via API in a single request up to a total of 1000 emails within 1 request, total request size cannot exceed 50mb

x-codeSamples.source:
import http.client

conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection("api.linkmobility.com")

payload = "[{\"recipient\":{\"to\":[{\"email\":\"string\",\"name\":\"string\"}],\"cc\":[{\"email\":\"string\",\"name\":\"string\"}],\"bcc\":[{\"email\":\"string\",\"name\":\"string\"}]},\"content\":{\"subject\":\"string\",\"body\":{\"text\":\"string\",\"html\":\"string\"},\"attachment\":[{\"contentType\":\"string\",\"filename\":\"string\",\"base64\":\"string\"}],\"options\":{\"email.sender\":{\"email\":\"string\",\"name\":\"string\"},\"email.replyTo\":{\"email\":\"string\",\"name\":\"string\"},\"email.tracking\":\"boolean\"}},\"expiration\":{\"relative\":1,\"absolute\":\"2019-08-24T14:15:22Z\"},\"callback\":{\"mode\":\"Profile\",\"urls\":[\"string\"],\"gateId\":\"string\",\"ttl\":28800000},\"referenceId\":\"string\",\"priority\":\"Normal\"}]"

headers = {
    'content-type': "application/json",
    'Authorization': "Bearer REPLACE_BEARER_TOKEN"
    }

conn.request("POST", "/email/v1/messages", payload, headers)

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

print(data.decode("utf-8"))

HttpResponse<String>response = Unirest.post("https://api.linkmobility.com/email/v1/messages")
  .header("content-type", "application/json")
  .header("Authorization", "Bearer REPLACE_BEARER_TOKEN")
  .body("[{\"recipient\":{\"to\":[{\"email\":\"string\",\"name\":\"string\"}],\"cc\":[{\"email\":\"string\",\"name\":\"string\"}],\"bcc\":[{\"email\":\"string\",\"name\":\"string\"}]},\"content\":{\"subject\":\"string\",\"body\":{\"text\":\"string\",\"html\":\"string\"},\"attachment\":[{\"contentType\":\"string\",\"filename\":\"string\",\"base64\":\"string\"}],\"options\":{\"email.sender\":{\"email\":\"string\",\"name\":\"string\"},\"email.replyTo\":{\"email\":\"string\",\"name\":\"string\"},\"email.tracking\":\"boolean\"}},\"expiration\":{\"relative\":1,\"absolute\":\"2019-08-24T14:15:22Z\"},\"callback\":{\"mode\":\"Profile\",\"urls\":[\"string\"],\"gateId\":\"string\",\"ttl\":28800000},\"referenceId\":\"string\",\"priority\":\"Normal\"}]")
  .asString();

curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.linkmobility.com/email/v1/messages \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_BEARER_TOKEN' \
  --header 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data '[{"recipient":{"to":[{"email":"string","name":"string"}],"cc":[{"email":"string","name":"string"}],"bcc":[{"email":"string","name":"string"}]},"content":{"subject":"string","body":{"text":"string","html":"string"},"attachment":[{"contentType":"string","filename":"string","base64":"string"}],"options":{"email.sender":{"email":"string","name":"string"},"email.replyTo":{"email":"string","name":"string"},"email.tracking":"boolean"}},"expiration":{"relative":1,"absolute":"2019-08-24T14:15:22Z"},"callback":{"mode":"Profile","urls":["string"],"gateId":"string","ttl":28800000},"referenceId":"string","priority":"Normal"}]'

Status code
CodeNameDescriptionStatus Group
successMessage delivered. 2000
connmaxoutGreenArrow’s throttling prevent a message from being sent. 5001
deferralMessage sending is being postponed. 5002
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 0
Bounce: hard		Non-bounceThis occurs when the bounce processor receives an email that it cannot classify as a bounce or any other non-bounce code 4000
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 10
Bounce: hard		Bad email addressThis is a hard bounce where we were able to positively identify that delivery attempts to this email address should no longer be attempted. This usually indicates that the requested mailbox does not exist. 3004
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 20
Bounce: soft		Temp failure - GeneralThis is a soft bounce which indicates a possibly temporary failure in delivery of the message. The email address itself may or may not be invalid. This is often the result of ambiguous messages such as a mailbox being “inactive” or “unavailable”. 5003
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 21
Bounce: soft		Temp failure - DNS FailureThis is a soft bounce caused by a failed DNS lookup. This can be caused by failures in DNS lookup either by GreenArrow itself or subsequent relay servers. 5004
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 22
Bounce: soft		Temp failure - Mailbox fullThis is a soft bounce caused by the recipient’s mailbox or quota being full. 5005
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 23
Bounce: other		Temp failure - Message size too largeThis is an other bounce caused by the destination email server rejecting the message due to its size. 4012
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 24
Bounce: soft		Temp failure - Missing MX recordThis system is configured with bounce_recipients_with_no_mx and no MX records were found for this recipient. 5006
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 29
Bounce: soft		Temp failure - Unable to connectThis is a soft bounce where we were unable to connect to the remote server. If there are many bounces with this code for a single domain, this usually means that the domain is not working or that the domain is blocking your mail server. 5007
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 30
Bounce: other		Bounce with no email addressThis is an other bounce caused by the bounce message itself containing no email address. Since our return paths include sufficient information to identify the recipient’s email address, GreenArrow no longer categorises any bounces as a 30.4021
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 40
Bounce: other		General bounceThis is an other bounce that could not otherwise be categorised. GreenArrow positively identified that this is a bounce message, but was unable to determine a more specific category. 4022
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 50
Bounce: other		Mail block - GeneralThis is an other bounce caused by the remote server rejecting the message for reasons that are not otherwise covered by a more specific “Mail block” category. 4023
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 51
Bounce: other		Mail block - Known SpammerThis is an other bounce caused by the remote server rejecting the message because it considers the sender to be a spammer. These bounces are not specific to the individual message, but rather the sending server itself. This can be caused by listing on various public or private block lists.td> 4013
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 52
Bounce: other		Mail block - Spam detectedThis is an other bounce caused by the remote server rejecting the individual message content as spam. 4020
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 53
Bounce: other		Mail block - Attachment detectedThis is an other bounce caused by the remote server rejecting the individual message due to its inclusion of one or more attachments.4014
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 54
Bounce: other		Mail block - Relay deniedThis is an other bounce caused by the remote server refusing to serve as a relay for delivery of the message.4015
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 55
Bounce: other		Mail block - SPF / DKIM / DMARCThis is an other bounce caused by the remote server refusing delivery of the message due to SPF, DKIM, or DMARC policies. Resolving the specific complaint in the bounce message can often improve deliverability. 4016
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 6059
Bounce: other		Mail block - Unable to connectThis is an other bounce where we were unable to connect to the remote server (much like code 29), however, this is to a large domain name, so we are reasonably confident that the domain name did not cease to exist, but that they are blocking all connections from your IP address. Some large domains, when blacklisting, will completely block your IP from connecting to their servers. 4017
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 60
Bounce: other		Auto-replyThese are messages received by the bounce processor that were generated by an auto-reply system such as a vacation autoresponder. These are not actual bounces. 2003
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 9070
Bounce: other		Transient bounceThis is an other bounce caused by a temporary delay in message transmission. The remote server will usually continue trying to deliver the message for a limited period of time.5008
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 90
Bounce: other		Unsubscribe requestThis is a hard bounce caused by a request to unsubscribe from the mailing list. 6001
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 100
Bounce: other		Challenge responseThis is an other bounce caused by the remote server issuing a challenge-response probe. GreenArrow does not respond to these challenges.4024
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 110
Bounce: other		Over GreenArrow throttle limitThis bounce happens when a message has been in the queue past the queue_lifetime limit, is scheduled for a delivery attempt, but that delivery attempt can not be made because it would go over the configured throttle settings for that IP or Relay Server (a connmaxout failure). 3014
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 120
Bounce: other		Queue dumpedThis is a bounce where GreenArrow was told to dump the messages in the queue. All the messages dumped from the queue will bounce with this code. 4018
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 121
Bounce: other		Delivery paused then message expiredThis is a bounce where GreenArrow was told to pause delivery of messages in a queue. After the maximum retry time, the messages are bounced, and they are bounced with this code.4008
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 122
Bounce: other		Suppressed by System due to Subscriber InactivityThis is a bounce where GreenArrow suppressed sending to the recipient because they haven’t taken an action, such as clicking a link or loading images which signals engagement.4025
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 123
Bounce: other		Blocked due to System policy enforcementThis is a bounce where GreenArrow suppressed sending to the recipient because of an AUP violation or another policy issue. 4026
Status: failure / failure_toolong
Code: 124
Bounce: other		Blocked due to daily throttling limitThis is a bounce where GreenArrow suppressed sending this message because the sender has reached its daily throttling limit. 3009
Status: failure / failure_toolong

messageId.description: Unique Link Message ID generated as part of the processing the request.

name.description: Template parameter name. The name can only accept letters [a-z], numbers [0-9], dashes [-] and underscores [_].

urls.description: List of URLs to receive DLRs on. Mandatory when using mode "URL" - not relevant to any other modes.

gateId.description: The ID of the callback to be used. Can be set up in the Callbacks section of MyLINK portal. Mandatory when using mode "Gate" - not relevant to any other modes.

MessageCallbackMode.description: Choose how you want to receive your Delivery reports. Mode Profile sends any DLRs towards your default configuration in MyLINK portal), URL sends towards a list of urls provided in the request, Gate sends towards a referenced configuration from MyLINK portal, or None (no DLR is sent anywhere). Each mode requires different request parameters, refer to the fields below.

relative.description: Time specified in milliseconds of how long the message is supposed to live. The maximum value is 48 hours (172800000 milliseconds), which is also the default.

absolute.description: Absolute time specified of when this message should expire. ISO8601 formatted string in UTC.

MessagePriority.description: Set priority on your own messages. Priority only affects your own queue.

responses.200: Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully
